task.description: WF-01 Step 1: expand Stage 3 (instance-engine) into REQ-xxx entries in docs/requirements.yaml. S2 (REQ-022..REQ-042) is fully done, so S3 is now the active stage and is eligible for expansion per docs/migration/README.md's 'Requirement expansion' rule. Requirements: none expanded yet') to list the expanded requirement ids, matching how stage-2-event-store-definitions.md's header reads.
acceptance_criteria: Every new requirement has id, title, owner, status: pending, stage: S3, description, >=2 concrete acceptance_criteria, depends_on -- same schema and prose style as the existing REQ-022..REQ-042 S2 block (read several in full first; match their depth, R-Co-path citation habit, and explicit OPEN QUESTION flagging convention)

Scope covers R-Co's src/engine/ (11 files) as stage-3-instance-engine.md defines it, decomposed along R-Co's own EE-01..EE-12 requirement ids (see R-Co docs/requirements.yaml, which carries full per-requirement acceptance criteria, and src/design/engine.md whose sections map 1:1: EE-01 Start Instance, EE-02 Pure Transition Function, EE-03 Task Activation, EE-04 Complete Task, EE-05 Exclusive Gateway, EE-06 Parallel Split, EE-07 Parallel Join, EE-08 Cancellation, EE-09 Variable Scoping, EE-10 Execution Error Handling, EE-11 State Reconstruction, EE-12 Concurrent Instance Safety), plus the non-EE engine files: snapshot_writer.zig (ISS-601 periodic state snapshots), service_task.zig (EXT-01), plugin_interface.zig + plugin_registry.zig (EXT-03), pin_resolver.zig (PIN-01..04), pin_rebind.zig (PIN-05), lua_script_audit.zig (LUA-07 minimal audit path)

Each requirement is sized to ONE agent turn -- R-Co's engine is ~13k lines of Zig (instance.zig alone is 5,550 lines, transition.zig 3,323, reconstruction.zig 1,646), so a 1:1 file-to-requirement mapping is WRONG and would produce oversized entries. Split along behavioral seams (EE-* sections) and chain them via depends_on, exactly as the S2 block split src/definition/'s 16 files into 21 requirements

depends_on references are real and genuinely required: new S3 requirements will depend on shipped S2 ids (REQ-023/025/026 event store, REQ-027 definition core schema + instance_definition_snapshots, REQ-028/029 graph validators, REQ-030 definition store CRUD, REQ-032 sub-process interface definition-time half, REQ-033 definition snapshot store) and on each other. No orphaned ids

The existing early-code generalization path is addressed explicitly rather than ignored: stage-3-instance-engine.md instructs that this stage GENERALIZES lib/letflow/process_instance.ex, lib/letflow/parallel_approval.ex, and lib/letflow/instance_supervisor.ex rather than starting fresh -- read all three modules first, and make the requirement(s) that supersede/absorb them say so concretely (which module is replaced, extended, or retired)

stage-3-instance-engine.md's two Early findings are honoured, not silently overridden: (1) hold the generalized engine to real :gen_statem per-state callbacks and real supervised isolation, not a GenServer hand-simulating a state machine; (2) do NOT assume process-per-instance by default -- the finding says its case is strongest for service task dispatch, plugin registries, timers, backpressure, and expensive-to-reconstruct in-memory state. Where a requirement faces the process-vs-row choice, flag it as an explicit OPEN QUESTION for CODE-DESIGNER (following the precedent set by REQ-039/REQ-040's descriptions) rather than pre-deciding it in the requirement text

No contradiction with any docs/migration/decisions/*.md record (read the directory: 0001-web-framework, 0002-oidc, 0003-ecto-schema-strategy, 0004-humanless-pipeline). In particular S3 tables must follow 0003 + REQ-022's schema-per-tenant mechanism unless there is a stated, R-Co-grounded reason to classify one as GLOBAL -- and if so, flag it as an OPEN QUESTION the way REQ-041's description does

Requirements stay inside S3's scope boundary: HTTP routes/controllers belong to S4 (api-surface), and the actual Lua/WASM runtime hosts belong to S5 (scripting-and-plugins). lua_script_audit.zig's engine-side audit path and plugin_registry/plugin_interface's registry contract ARE in S3, but the script/plugin execution runtimes they call into are NOT -- state that boundary explicitly in the affected requirements
Append-only: do not reorder, rewrite, or renumber any existing requirement entry
Report the full list of new REQ ids with one-line titles in your handoff result summary, plus explicitly note any R-Co engine behavior you deliberately deferred out of S3 and why
